newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil current account pressured by trade,services.
newsitem.headline: Brazil current account pressured by trade,services.

text.p: An erosion in 1996 of Brazil's current account gap compared with the previous year was due to a "worse-than-expected" trade deficit and a widening in the services deficit, said a Central Bank official.
Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said the services account posted a shortfall of $21.707 billion against $18.6 billion in 1995.
"In addition, we had fewer unilateral transfers (from Brazilians living abroad)," Lopes told reporters.
Brazil had a current account deficit of $24.3 billion or 3.27 percent of gross domestic product in 1996. In 1995, the deficit was $17.742 billion or 2.47 percent of GDP.
Last year's trade deficit was $5.54 billion compared with $3.352 billion the previous year.

On the services accounts, the deficit in interest payments rose in 1996 to $9.84 billion from $8.158 billion while the shortfall on international travel -- what Brazilians spend abroad -- surged to $3.593 billion from $2.419 billion.
Unilateral transfers, mainly from "kasseguis", Brazilian Japanese living in Japan, slumped to $2.899 billion in 1996 from $3.973 billion in 1995.

According to Lopes, the drop in the transfers was due to the yen currency's weakness against the dollar, tighter controls on remittances and also the fact that state-run Banco do Brasil has started raising funds in Japan.
